final_recommendation: Credit Suisse draws CHF 100B SNB liquidity tonight, posts it visibly before Asia opens, and commits to operating independently Monday through Friday with no acquisition contingencies. Federal Council and SNB issue joint statement affirming CHF 150B floor (CHF 100B liquidity + CHF 50B loss protection) that holds regardless of transaction status. SNB issues technical letter confirming AT1 statutory subordination under Article 36, but Federal Council refuses to pre-commit AT1 hierarchy in writing to avoid litigation exposure.
minority_objections: UBS CEO demands written AT1 subordination locked into transaction docs before signing any Monday deal, rejected by Federal Council as premature legal commitment
AT1 rep demands explicit written protection inside CHF 150B floor, rejected as politically and legally untenable
Wealth client and creditors demand visible proof of independence beyond liquidity draw—capital actions, client comms, operational continuity—not delivered by meeting end
key_conflicts: Federal Council vs UBS/AT1 creditors: Federal Council refuses all written AT1 subordination commitments to avoid pre-deciding hierarchy and litigation risk; UBS and creditors demand written clarity to stop deposit flight
Independence vs acquisition ambiguity: CS CEO commits to standalone operation through Friday, but creditors and UBS assume forced sale by Wednesday if deposits continue bleeding
Legal defensibility vs market confidence: every attempt to clarify AT1 treatment rejected as creating litigation exposure, leaving creditors uncertain and still running
key_concessions: Federal Council commits CHF 150B floor unconditional and binding on any transaction structure—major public sector exposure locked before deal terms negotiated
SNB issues Article 36 technical letter affirming statutory AT1 subordination—modest legal clarity without policy pre-commitment
CS CEO commits to full operating plan Monday-Friday with zero acquisition contingencies—independence signal without visible proof
red_lines: Federal Council: no written AT1 subordination in any government statement or transaction docs before deal exists—litigation and political exposure unacceptable
UBS CEO: no acquisition without written AT1 hierarchy locked into transaction structure—board won't sign without loss protection
SNB: CHF 150B floor must be ironclad in Federal Council writing before structuring any loss hierarchy—cannot risk floor reinterpretation post-transaction
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Visible proof of independence: creditors demand concrete Monday actions (capital raise, client retention, operational hires) but CS provides only commitment language—no tangible signal delivered
Wednesday CET1 trajectory: CS claims 13.5% Monday holds above 12% Wednesday even with continued bleeding, but no stress test presented and creditors remain skeptical
Litigation inevitability: Federal Council assumes avoiding written AT1 language prevents litigation, but creditors signal they will litigate ambiguity anyway—silence may be worse than clarity
downstream_risk_variables: Monday deposit flows: entire independence path depends on whether CHF 100B draw actually stops bleeding—no Plan B if it fails
UBS deal terms: if forced to buyer by Wednesday, AT1 hierarchy still unresolved and will require emergency negotiation under time pressure
AT1 creditor litigation: regardless of weekend outcome, creditors signal legal challenge to any hierarchy interpretation—litigation risk deferred, not avoided
uncertainty_notes: Meeting ends with liquidity draw executed and independence committed, but no visible proof of operational continuity delivered to creditors. Federal Council's refusal to clarify AT1 treatment in writing leaves capital structure hierarchy unresolved. CS claims 13.5% CET1 holds through Wednesday, but creditors remain unconvinced deposits will stabilize. If Monday deposit flows do not improve, forced acquisition by midweek with AT1 hierarchy still contested and litigation inevitable.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Drove the CHF 150B structure: CHF 100B liquidity alone insufficient, forced addition of CHF 50B loss floor and Federal Council backstop as binding constraint on solution
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: Discussed extensively as contingency if deposits continue bleeding, but explicitly rejected as primary path—CS CEO commits to independence Monday-Friday with no acquisition contingencies
marker_evidence.government_support: Decisive: CHF 150B Federal Council/SNB commitment became the binding floor, unconditional and locked before any transaction terms negotiated—shaped entire rescue structure
marker_evidence.client_flight: Decisive: deposit bleeding drove every decision—liquidity draw timing, statement language, independence commitment all designed to stop the run before Monday open
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: Decisive: AT1 subordination question dominated rounds 5-10, forced SNB Article 36 letter, blocked multiple proposals, became the unresolved constraint preventing full creditor confidence
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: Decisive: Federal Council vs UBS/creditors deadlock over written AT1 hierarchy—Federal Council's refusal to commit in writing became binding red line that left capital structure unresolved
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: Raised repeatedly as reason Federal Council rejected all written AT1 commitments, but did not force a concrete alternative solution—acknowledged as inevitable but deferred
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Raised as constraint on statement timing and legal review, but did not materially change the decision—authorities met the weekend deadline with liquidity draw and statement
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Raised as reason for urgency and visible cash draw before Asia open, but the specific Monday panic scenario did not drive the structure—liquidity draw would have happened regardless
